title: QVC Group starts over in West Chester after shedding $5 billion in debt
summary: The Wilson Drive shopping network left Chapter 11 on Aug. 6 with its long-term debt cut from $6.6 billion to $1.3 billion, a new $600 million lending facility and a Nasdaq listing under QVCG. Former chief Mike George has returned as board chairman and interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent leader.

title: Borough signs off on West Chester University's campus master plan
summary: Council approved the university's 800-page master plan with conditions after more than a year of negotiation over student housing, parking and public-realm changes. The plan sets the framework borough officials will measure future campus projects against.

title: Draft 2027 budget swaps the repealed stormwater fee for a tax increase
summary: Borough staff presented a 2027 budget Tuesday, Sept. 15 that raises property taxes to replace the roughly $1.2 million a year lost when the Stream Protection Fee was repealed. Borough Manager Sean Mettrick put the typical household's current tax-and-fee bill near $2,200, and the borough posted an online tool for comparing the old fee with the proposed tax.

title: 45th Restaurant and Food Truck Festival fills downtown Sunday
summary: The free festival runs noon to 5:30 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 20 across downtown West Chester, with more than 50 food vendors and restaurants, 80-plus crafters, three stages of live music and a beer and wine garden on North Church Street. The rain date is Sunday, Sept. 27.

title: Two brothers are the first through WCU's fast-track quantum degree
summary: Michael and Tyler Manfre became the inaugural pair to finish a 3+2 pathway that pairs a three-year physics bachelor's at West Chester University with a two-year master's in quantum science and engineering at the University of Delaware. Both have since started engineering jobs at Oxford Instruments and CACI International.

title: WCU opens its fall sustainability tours and talks to the public
summary: West Chester University's free fall lineup includes weekly Wednesday research seminars starting Sept. 23, a green-roof tour at The Commons on Sept. 22, later tours of North Campus, the Gordon Natural Area and the geothermal pumphouse, and an Oct. 22 community panel on plastics and health at 50 Sharpless St.

title: New assistant principals start at Henderson and Fugett
summary: The West Chester Area School Board approved Jackie Longan, a former Downingtown gifted-education specialist, as assistant principal at Henderson High School and Amy Terkanian, a longtime Garnet Valley math educator, for the same role at Fugett Middle School. Both bring about two decades in the classroom.

title: Chester County measles cases reach 65 as state deaths hit four
summary: Chester County added nine measles cases in a week to reach 65 confirmed, part of a statewide count of 693 that health officials call Pennsylvania's worst outbreak in more than three decades. The state confirmed two more deaths, bringing the year's toll to four.

title: Netflix's 'Tires' co-creator still calls West Chester home
summary: Steve Gerben, who co-created and stars in the Netflix comedy Tires alongside Shane Gillis, films the show in an addition to his father's former tire shop on East Gay Street and golfs weekly on West Chester courses. The series was renewed for a fourth season after its Aug. 13 season-three premiere drew 2.4 million views in its first weekend.

title: West Chester starts enforcing its 35-gallon trash can limit after Sept. 30
summary: The borough's updated garbage ordinance caps curbside trash cans at 35 gallons, and Public Works says larger cans will stop being collected once a grace period ends Sept. 30, with fines possible after that. The borough says it has no approved alternative for households that need bigger containers.
